data.gender_notes: Marzi is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'r-z-y', meaning 'graceful' or 'delicate'. This name is mentioned in various Hadiths and is associated with noble character and beautiful manners. The name Marzi carries the meaning “Graceful, Delicate” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Marzi usually hope their child will grow to embody graceful, delicate and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_arabic.name: مرزي
in_arabic.meaning: اسم يعني المرغوب فيه أو المطلوب
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم مرزي مشتق من الجذر العربي م-ر-ز، ويعني المرغوب فيه أو المطلوب، وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم في عدة مواضع، منها قوله تعالى: 'فَمَرْزُ القَلبِ مِنَ النَظَرِ إلَى المُحَرَّمِ وَاجِبٌ'، ويحمل الاسم دلالات روحية عميقة تتعلق بالإرادة والرغبة في القلب.

in_urdu.name: مرزی
in_urdu.meaning: مرغوب میں یا ضروری کے معنی
in_urdu.long_meaning: مرزی نام عربی جڑ م-ر-ز سے نکلا ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے مرغوب میں یا ضروری، یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں کے درمیان میں مقبول ہے اور اسلامی روایت میں اس کی اہمیت ہے، خاص طور پر دل کی خواہشوں اور ضروریات کے سلسلے میں.

in_hindi.name: मरज़ी

in_pashto.name: مرزی

historical_references.reference: Marziyah bint al-Hakam was a prominent Islamic scholar and the first female jurist in Islamic history. She was born in Damascus, Syria around 661 CE and studied under well-known scholars of her time, including her father, al-Hakam ibn Amr. She later became a teacher and transmitted knowledge to many students. Her expertise in Islamic law led her to be consulted by caliphs and other rulers for legal opinions.
historical_references.context: Studies and contributes to Islamic scholarship as a female jurist

historical_references.reference: Marziyya ibn Muhammad al-Qurashi was a Sufi Saint and poet from Shiraz, Iran in the 13th century CE. She is known for her poetry, which expresses her love for God and her spiritual experiences. Her poetry was highly regarded by other Sufi poets and scholars of her time, and she is still remembered and revered in the Sufi tradition today.
